angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 824,405 km at 171.61 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.8273 +/- 0.0169 mas (same row, RUWE 0.95): 171.61 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.185 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Nascimbeni et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-24 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A.349N/abstract): 824,405 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.091 +/- 0.056 solar masses from Nascimbeni et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-24 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A.349N/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5726 +/- 65 K from Nascimbeni et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-24 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A.349N/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Nascimbeni et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-24 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A.349N/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-24.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.328, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
